\section{Overview}

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-Time Reduction from a Language in P]
\lean{Randomized.polyTimeReducible_of_mem_P}
\label{Randomized.polyTimeReducible_of_mem_P}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.mem_P_iff_polyTimeComputable, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_const, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_ite, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{4}
Let $L$ and $L'$ be languages of finite binary strings, with $L'\in\mathsf{P}$. If there
are binary strings $a\in L$ and $b\notin L$, then $L'$ is polynomial-time many-one
reducible to $L$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[No reduction from the universal language to empty]
\lean{Randomized.not_polyTimeReducible_empty}
\label{Randomized.not_polyTimeReducible_empty}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
There is no polynomial-time many-one reduction from the language of all finite binary
strings to the empty language of binary strings.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[No reduction from empty language to universal]
\lean{Randomized.not_polyTimeReducible_univ}
\label{Randomized.not_polyTimeReducible_univ}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
There is no polynomial-time many-one reduction from the empty language of binary strings
to the language of all finite binary strings.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Language containing only the empty word]
\lean{Randomized.emptyWordLang}
\label{Randomized.emptyWordLang}
\leanok
Over the Boolean alphabet, the language consists exactly of the empty word.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The empty-word language is in polynomial time]
\lean{Randomized.emptyWordLang_mem_P}
\label{Randomized.emptyWordLang_mem_P}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.mem_P_iff_polyTimeComputable, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_isNil, Randomized.emptyWordLang, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{4}
The language consisting exactly of the empty binary string belongs to the class of
polynomial-time decidable binary languages.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reduction to the empty-word language]
\lean{Randomized.polyTimeReducible_emptyWordLang}
\label{Randomized.polyTimeReducible_emptyWordLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Randomized.emptyWordLang, Randomized.polyTimeReducible_of_mem_P}
\difficulty{1}
Let $L'$ be a language over the binary alphabet that belongs to polynomial time. Then
$L'$ is polynomial-time reducible to the language whose only word is the empty word.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Existence of a randomized hard language]
\lean{Randomized.exists_BPPHard_mem_BPP_PTM_of_eq_P}
\label{Randomized.exists_BPPHard_mem_BPP_PTM_of_eq_P}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Randomized.BPPHard, Randomized.BPP_PTM, Randomized.emptyWordLang, Randomized.emptyWordLang_mem_P, Randomized.polyTimeReducible_emptyWordLang}
\difficulty{3}
Assume that the class of languages decidable in polynomial time with bounded error
equals the class of languages decidable in deterministic polynomial time. Then there is
a language in the bounded-error probabilistic polynomial-time class to which every
language in that class is polynomial-time many-one reducible.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomized polynomial time under P equals BPP]
\lean{Randomized.BPP_PTM_ssubset_DTIME_pow_log_of_eq_P}
\label{Randomized.BPP_PTM_ssubset_DTIME_pow_log_of_eq_P}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Complexity.P, Randomized.BPP_PTM, Randomized.P_ssubset_DTIME_pow_log}
\difficulty{1}
Assume that the class of languages decidable by bounded-error randomized polynomial-time
machines equals the class decidable by deterministic polynomial-time machines. Then the
bounded-error randomized polynomial-time class is a proper subset of the languages
decidable in time $n^{\log_2 n}$.
\end{theorem}
